items.title: How long does the study last?
items.content: The minimum participation we need is 3 months. But there is an option for a possible extension up to 12 months.

items.title: How do I take part?
items.content:
To take part, you need to:
  • Check your eligibility.
  • Read the Participant Information Sheet.
  • Provide electronic consent.
  • Install the apps and begin participation.

items.title: What will I need to do?
items.content:
Wear Your Wearable Device: We will ask you to wear your fitness tracker or smart device as much as possible during the study (for at least 3 months, optionally up to 12 months).
You will need to install:
  • RADAR Passive App (used to monitor your data)
  • RADAR Active App (send short daily and weekly questionnaires, taking around 2-3 minutes).

Take a Cognitive Test: You will be invited to complete short online cognitive tasks using the Cognitron platform to explore how sleep and phone use relate to attention and thinking performance.

items.title: What wearable can I use?
items.content: The devices that are compatible are Fitbit, Oura Ring, Garmin, Apple Watch, Polar, Empatica E4.

items.title: What smartphone can I use?
items.content: You must have an Android mobile device with version 5.1 or later or Apple mobile device with iOS version 14 or later

items.title: What will happen to the data?
items.content:
Your data will be:
  • Analysed to understand patterns of smartphone use and sleep.
  • Used to publish scientific findings (you will never be identifiable).
  • Potentially shared in de-identified form with approved researchers worldwide (if you consent).
  • You may choose whether or not your anonymised data can be shared for future research.

items.title: How is my data protected?
items.content:
Your privacy is extremely important to us.
  • Your data is processed in accordance with the UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 where all data are de-identified using a unique study ID.
  • Your name and contact details are stored separately and securely.
  • We do not access the content of messages or calls Relative location data are offset to prevent identification.

King’s College London is the study sponsor and data controller.

items.title: Are there any risks?
items.content:
Risks are minimal.
  • The study requires a small amount of time for questionnaires.
  • There is a very small cybersecurity risk similar to everyday smartphone use.
  • If you feel uncomfortable with our data collection — you may withdraw at any time with/without giving a reason. You may request deletion of identifiable data within the first 30 days.
